items.markdown: **A step can have its own key that turns it off and on.** Right-click a step, choose Set Toggle Key and press the key you want. Out of combat that key turns the step off or back on at once, and chat names the step and the sequence. In combat it changes nothing and says so. `/gems stepkey` sets, clears and lists these keys, which is also how to reach them in Simplified Mode. Each character keeps its own step keys. A key that is already bound to something is refused, and if you later give that key to a sequence or to something in the game's key bindings, that wins and chat tells you.

items.markdown: **With no recommendation for a sequence, every variant slot sits at full brightness.** They were all dimmed instead. Dimming means there is advice and this slot is not the one it points at. Before, having no advice looked exactly like advice against everything.

items.markdown: **Turning on Right Click, Middle Click, Mouse Button 4 or Mouse Button 5 as a reset modifier now tells you how to use it.** A keybind press never counts as one of those clicks, and neither does clicking the sequence's macro, because the macro only ever sends a left click. Through a keybind or the macro, these four never reset a sequence. They do reset it when a macro line of your own clicks the sequence with that mouse button. When you turn one on in the sequence editor, the chat line shows the exact line to put in that macro.

items.markdown: **You can no longer rename a sequence in combat, the same as deleting one.** A rename in combat left the old name in your list until the changes waiting for combat to end were applied, and renaming it again from there gave you two copies of the sequence. A rename is also refused while an activation of that sequence queued in combat hasn't run yet, because it could bring the old name back. With Auto-reload sequences at combat end turned off, it waits until you run `/gems apply`. Either way chat says why.

items.markdown: **The keybind conflict panel's Fix now asks first when it would switch off a macro branch.** The panel clears a cast redirect by setting Self Cast, Focus Cast or Mouseover Cast to None. That also stops every branch that checks the same setting, such as `[mod:SELFCAST]`, in any of your sequences. With account-wide key bindings the setting is shared, so it stops those branches on your other characters that use account-wide bindings too. Fix All doesn't touch those rows any more, and a row's own Fix names the setting and the sequences that use it and asks before it changes anything. Another character's sequences are named as they were the last time you logged in on it, and only once you've logged in on it with this version. A character on another realm is named with its realm.

It's still fine to ask such a tool for help installing or using your own copy. AGENTS.md, a short notice for automated readers, now ships beside it. Nothing about how you use the addon changes.

items.markdown: **The `UnitHealthPercent` variable helper is gone.** It read your health as a number and the game no longer lets an addon do that. Instead of failing it had been handing back 0, so a variable built on it gave a wrong answer and nothing said so. That variable now evaluates to nothing. With debug output turned on EMS names the missing helper in the log. There is no replacement and there cannot be one, because nothing an addon can call turns your health back into a number it is allowed to compare. The variable helpers that still work in combat answer true or false. They are `HasBuff`, `HasDebuff`, `SpellReady`, `SpellOnCooldown`, `SpellEnabled` and `IsRestricted`. A banded companion to `UnitHealthPercent` was added after v2.4.20 and goes with it. No released build carried that one.

items.markdown: **Reset modifiers and reset timers now work.** Holding a modifier you had set to send a sequence back to step 1 did nothing at all: the press cast nothing and the step did not move. A reset timer never fired either, though those presses cast normally. Both went through a button attribute the game refuses to let a sequence read or write. That attribute has a name the game accepts now, and the gap is measured before the press instead of after it, so coming back after a long pause puts you on step 1 on the very first press. A pause that ends while you are in combat is held until the fight is over, so your next press after that starts from step 1 wherever it happens, and it is dropped if you go back to pressing during the fight, because at that point you have not paused. Every other kind of reset was unaffected throughout: leaving combat, changing target, swapping gear, changing specialisation, and the manual reset.

Holding a modifier could still cast the old version's variant steps, and a variant only the new version has was missing.

items.markdown: **Set Default and Delete Version now switch the steps a sequence casts.** Switching to a version with no steps left the sequence casting the old version's steps until you reloaded. The other way round, from an empty version to one with steps, the keybind did nothing until you reloaded. A version with fewer steps could cast one of the old version's steps on the next press and then skip step 1. These switches now rebuild the sequence and start it at step 1, as a reload does, and so does any switch to a version with a different number of steps or a different Step Function. Switching between two versions with the same number of steps and the same Step Function keeps your place, as before. After either button a context override could also be ignored, so entering a dungeon whose override named another version kept the sequence where it was until you reloaded. That override takes effect now.

items.markdown: **Switching a sequence's Step Function from Priority or Reverse Priority to Sequential no longer repeats a cast.** Priority and Reverse Priority repeat your steps, so they have more of them to walk through than Sequential does. If you had pressed far enough into the sequence, the switch left it past its new last step. The next press then cast the same step as the press before it, and the sequence could go on to skip its first steps. It now goes back to step 1 when that happens, and so do its variants. A sequence still on one of its steps stays where it is.

items.markdown: **Pinning a version or entering a context now changes what the sequence casts.** A pin or a context override onto a version with no steps, or clearing a pin when the default version has no steps, left the sequence casting the old version's steps until you reloaded. The other way round, from an empty version to one with steps, the keybind did nothing until you reloaded. Switching away from a damaged default version onto one without variants did the same, and so did Set Default. Pinning or switching context between a Random version and a version with any other Step Function kept the old version's behaviour, so the Random version walked its steps in order or the other version picked them at random. These switches now rebuild the sequence the way a reload does. One kind of damaged Step Function setting, which only an import or another addon can store, made a pin or a context switch onto that version stop with an error and keep the old steps. It now plays the version in order. `/gems reset` typed in combat before a switch that rebuilds the sequence now resets the rebuilt button. It used to leave the macro icon showing the old version's first step until your next press.

items.markdown: **Switching to a version with a raid marker in its steps no longer keeps casting the version you left.** The game will not load a sequence step that contains a curly brace, and a raid marker such as `{rt8}` in a `/yell` line is written with two, so a version holding one cannot run. Pinning that version, entering a context that uses it, clearing a pin back to it, Set Default and Delete Version all left the sequence casting the old version. After Set Default or Delete Version, a modifier variant whose new steps hold a marker also kept its old steps. The sequence now behaves as it does after a reload, and its keybind casts nothing for that version until the marker is taken out. Saving an edit that adds a marker to a step used to keep casting the step as it was before the edit. It now casts nothing as well.

items.markdown: **A sequence that embeds another now keeps up with it.** Editing the embedded sequence left the one embedding it casting the old steps until something rebuilt it. Logging in could drop the embedded steps altogether. Whether it did came down to the order the game handed your sequences back, and the shortened copy was then saved over yours. A sequence that embeds itself grew by one copy of its own steps every time it was rebuilt, and a save was enough to do that. Two sequences that embed each other grew the same way. Now every sequence that embeds another is rebuilt when that one's steps change, and starts again from step 1. An edit that leaves the steps as they were, such as a Key Press change, doesn't send it back to step 1. An embed that leads back to the sequence it sits in adds nothing, and the rest of that sequence plays as normal.

items.markdown: **Switching to a damaged version now does what a reload does.** An import or another addon can store a version that isn't a real version at all. Pinning one, entering a context set to one, or clearing a pin when the default is one left the sequence casting the version it was on, from the step it had reached. The editor already showed the new version as live. After a reload that keybind casts nothing, and the switch now does the same. Modifier variants from the old version are removed too. A version stored past the end of the version list, such as version 7 on a sequence with two, was skipped as well. Clearing a pin onto it or entering a context set to it kept the old version casting. It now switches to that version and starts at step 1, as a reload does.

items.markdown: **A version switch made in combat now holds when combat ends.** If something had asked a sequence to rebuild its steps earlier in the same fight, such as a change to one of its variables, pinning a version, clearing a pin or entering a context was undone when combat ended. The sequence went back to casting the old version's steps, and its macro kept the old version's Key Press. Set Default in the same situation, between a Random version and one with another Step Function, left the old Key Press in the macro. Both lasted until the sequence was next rebuilt, for example by a reload. The version you switched to now stays in place.

The sequence now stays in your list and stays disabled.

items.markdown: **Saving a sequence twice in one fight no longer loses the second save.** A save that changes the number of steps or the Step Function waits for combat to end before it takes effect. If you saved again before then, and that second save had the same number of steps and the same Step Function the sequence had before the fight, the first save replaced it when combat ended. The first save is also what stayed in your saved sequences. A save made after you disabled and re-enabled the sequence in the same fight was lost the same way. Your second save is the one that stays now. A save that waits for combat to end is also written to your saved sequences straight away, so a reload before the fight is over keeps it.

Ctrl and Alt variants had the same problem. A variant now doesn't count the reset modifiers its own key holds down, and every other reset modifier still sends it back to step 1. Turning on a reset modifier that a variant ignores now says so in chat.

Turning Left Click on now says so in chat.

items.markdown: **Modifier variants now work on a keybind that already has a modifier in it.** A Shift variant on a key with Ctrl or Alt in it, such as Ctrl+4, never fired, and neither did a Ctrl variant on a key with Alt in it. EMS bound them under a name the game never matches. They're bound the way the game names the key now. A variant whose modifier is already part of the key, such as a Ctrl variant on Ctrl+4, would be the same key twice, so it isn't bound and the key keeps playing the sequence. A key typed into `/gems bind` with its modifiers in another order, such as `shift-ctrl-4`, never fired either, and it works now unless another sequence is already bound to that key. Keys without a modifier are bound exactly as before. If a sequence's own key holds a modifier you have set to reset that sequence, every press starts it again at step 1, and EMS now says so in chat.

Shift+4 now always plays the sequence you bound to it, and that Shift variant has no key until one of the two keybinds changes. The Keybind tab tells you when the key you're setting is another sequence's variant key.

items.markdown: **A damaged reset-modifier setting on one sequence no longer breaks reset-modifier changes, version switches or the editor.** If a stored version's reset modifiers had been damaged, changing a reset modifier in the settings panel, or switching profile, stopped with an error at that sequence, and the change didn't reach the sequences after it. Switching to that version, by pin or by context, stopped the same way and left the sequence casting the old version's steps. Both now fall back to the global reset modifiers for that version. Saving, renaming or duplicating the sequence, or duplicating that version, also stopped with an error. Opening that version in the editor could stop part way through, or show a per-sequence setting with every modifier off. The editor now shows the global reset modifiers for it, which is what that version uses, and saving the sequence clears the damaged setting. The Repair panel lists it too, with a fix that clears it.

items.markdown: **A recommend function written the way the Insert Helper writes it now runs.** The picker inserts a helper as `GRIPEMS.HasBuff(0, "player")`. Variables understood that form and recommendations did not, so a recommendation built from a picker snippet failed on its first line and never lit anything. With debug output off, which is how it ships, nothing in chat said why. Recommendations read the same form as variables now. The plugin condition call `GRIPEMS.API:EvaluateCondition("id")` reached neither before and works in both now. The plugin documentation only ever shows it inside a variable body, and that is the case that was broken.

items.markdown: **A variable that calls one of the macro conditional helpers in a shape EMS cannot bake no longer comes out blank.** Helpers such as `GRIPEMS.InCombat` normally become a native conditional that the game reads as you press. Where the shape around one is not something EMS can turn into a conditional, the variable is worked out when the sequence is built instead, and that path did not know those helpers, so the variable put nothing at all into your macro. It puts its value in now. That value is settled when the sequence is built, so it holds until the sequence is built again. The six helpers the Insert Helper picker offers were never affected, because they have always been available on that path.

They go back to normal at once. Switching versions or reloading does not flash them, because a sequence that comes straight back is not treated as having gone away.

The overlay is drawn from the current advice every time it is redrawn. With the indicators off nothing is dimmed and no border is shown.

items.markdown: **Sequence names with a space in them now work in `/gems bind`, `/gems swap`, `/gems send` and `/gems variants`.** You can name a sequence `My Rotation` in the editor, but those four commands read the name only as far as the first space, so they went looking for a sequence called `My` and told you it did not exist. They read the whole name now. If you have both `My` and `My Rotation`, the longer one wins and `My` is still reachable on its own. Sending to another player was the worst of the four, because the error named a sequence you had not typed. Names without spaces behave exactly as they did before, and nothing about the way names are stored has changed.

items.markdown: **A context switch no longer stops partway when one sequence fails to reload.** Entering a dungeon reloads the sequences whose context override names another version. If one of those reloads stopped with an error, every sequence due after it kept casting its old version until you reloaded. Each one reloads on its own now, and with debug output turned on EMS names the sequence that failed. One way to hit it was an If block holding an Embed of a sequence with a damaged step, which only an import or another addon can store. The sequence holding that If block also failed to load. The damaged step is now left out of the Embed, and the embedded sequence's other steps play as before. A step stored as a list of lines is not left out: the Embed casts its lines.

items.markdown: **Disabling a plugin now takes its sequences off the plugin's Step Function straight away.** A sequence whose Step Function came from a plugin kept casting in that plugin's order after the plugin was disabled. It went on doing so until you reloaded or the sequence was next rebuilt, and that rebuild could repeat the previous cast on one press before the sequence started over. The sequence now plays its steps in order from step 1 as soon as the plugin is disabled. Turning the plugin back on returns it to the plugin's order from step 1, which used to wait for a reload.

Each kind of rebuild now waits once, however many times it was asked for.

items.markdown: **Renaming a sequence now keeps all of its keybinds.** Only the key for your current spec and talent loadout moved to the new name. Keys saved for your other specs and loadouts stayed on the old name and did nothing, and they came back if you ever made a sequence with that name again. If the sequence was enabled, a rename made in combat lost even the current key, and chat said the sequence was not found. Every saved key now moves with the rename, straight away, and the chat line that used to confirm the one key it carried is gone.

items.markdown: **EMS no longer tells you your keybinds didn't load while they are only waiting for combat to end.** If EMS loaded none of your saved keybinds, for example right after a login, it checked again three seconds later. When you were in combat by then, that check could not load them, so it printed the message that says your keybinds didn't load and tells you to type `/gems binds restore`, and then the keybinds came back after the fight. The check now waits for the load to run, and only tells you if the keybinds are still missing after it.

items.markdown: **The keybind conflict panel now checks branches written with a modified-click action, such as `[mod:SELFCAST]`, and the key each modifier variant is bound to.** A branch like that runs while you hold the modifier the game's options give that action. The panel didn't read it, so a key taken by something else still showed as clear. When one was combined with another modifier, as in `[mod:SELFCAST,mod:ctrl]`, the panel checked the wrong key. A variant's own key, such as Shift+F3 for a Shift variant on F3, wasn't checked unless the sequence's own macro lines also branched on Shift.

A key taken by something else could still show as clear.

items.markdown: **A Repair fix for a sequence's macro now checks that sequence again when it runs.** The fixes for "Stub body out of sync" and "No keybind and no stub" kept the name and the lines the sequence had when the Repair panel showed it. Pressed on a Repair panel left open while you renamed or deleted the sequence, or pressed in combat and run after such a rename or delete with Auto-reload sequences at combat end turned off, they made a macro that clicked a button that no longer existed. If a new sequence had taken the old name, they rewrote its macro with the old sequence's lines instead. A fix that ran after you saved the sequence, pressed in combat or on a panel left open, also wrote its macro from the old lines. They now do nothing once the sequence they were built for is gone, and otherwise use it as it is when they run.

items.markdown: **The editor no longer stops part way through loading a sequence with a damaged date.** A sequence imported from a string could carry a created, updated, forked or last modified date that isn't a date at all, or fork and edit history stored in the wrong shape, and a plugin could hand EMS a created date like that too. Selecting such a sequence stopped the editor with an error after the name and details, and the steps and tabs below kept showing the sequence you had open before. The editor now leaves a damaged date blank and loads the rest. The author badge in the import preview had the same problem, in its hover details and in the full chain list a click on it opens, and is fixed too. The Last modified line no longer shows 1970-01-01 when no date was recorded, and shows ? when the name of whoever changed it is missing. A sequence a plugin adds shows no Created date, since plugins add their sequences again every session.

items.markdown: **A variable whose body starts with `return`, `local` or `if`, or wraps a plain expression in `function() ... end`, is no longer treated as broken.** EMS already used one like that when it could turn the variable into a macro conditional. Everywhere else it read the body as broken: the Variables tab marked it invalid, the Repair panel listed a parse error, importing one warned that its body was invalid, and a step that used it could cast nothing. It works in all of those now. One that wraps a single call in `function() ... end` was never flagged, but it gave nothing, so a step that used it cast nothing as well. It now gives what the call returns.

Tol'Viron Arena and Tiger's Peak were swapped. A version ticked for Ashamane's Fall ran in Blade's Edge Arena instead, and the same went for Hook Point in The Robodrome, Mugambala in Empyrean Domain and Empyrean Domain in Maldraxxus Coliseum. Ticking Blade's Edge Arena, Nagrand Arena, Maldraxxus Coliseum or The Robodrome did nothing. In battlegrounds, a version ticked for Silvershard Mines ran in Warsong Gulch, Seething Shore in Arathi Basin and Wintergrasp in Deepwind Gorge, and ticking Warsong Gulch, Arathi Basin or Deepwind Gorge did nothing. Map ticks still apply only in unrated arenas and battlegrounds.

items.markdown: **A sequence imported with damaged details no longer breaks the editor, the sequence list or sharing.** An import string can carry an author, a class, a description or a fork history in the wrong form, and EMS stored it exactly as it came. Selecting that sequence could stop the editor part way, a sequence list sorted by class could fail to draw, and sharing the sequence privately could stop with an error. EMS now keeps each of those details only when it has the right form, and puts right the ones already saved when you log in. If a sequence you imported was signed by an author who had saved its class, spec, icon, description, link or talent code in the wrong form, it now shows as Tampered, because the signature covers the form they saved. Sequences you wrote yourself are signed again instead.

That send also prints the import's warnings now. When a sequence in an EMS string uses a macro that the import doesn't make and you don't have, the import window, `/gems import` and a friend's auto-accepted send now name it.

items.markdown: **A legacy string imported through the import window or sent to you by another player gives its steps the macros it carries.** A legacy step can name a macro by its name alone. In v2.4.20 a step like that kept the name, which a press sends to chat, or took the text of a macro of your own with the same name. The import window also said the macro wasn't in the import, though the import made it. The step now gets the text of the macro the string carries, as `/gems import` already did. If you have a macro of your own with that name and the import leaves yours alone, the step still gets the string's text, and the step editor shows it out of sync with your macro. If you untick the macro, the step gets its text too, and the import names the macro as one it didn't make.

Every character now does it once more. A step, Key Press or Key Release that names a macro by its name alone gets the text of the macro EMS made for it or, if there isn't one, of your own macro with that name.

They now name the new one. A `/cast` line keeps the name, so a macro named like a spell doesn't stop that spell's casts.

It now counts up to a name no sequence of yours and no other sequence in the import uses, and the import window's row shows that name.

items.markdown: **Renaming a macro in the import window no longer renames a spell in an EMS string.** The rename moved every whole word that matched the macro's name, so with a macro named like a spell, such as Charge renamed to Charge (2), each `/cast Charge` in the steps became `/cast Charge (2)` and cast nothing. Now a line moves only where it runs the macro: a line that is the macro's name alone, or the name after `/click`, in a step, the Key Press or the Key Release. Steps in an action sequence kept the old name, so they clicked your own macro of that name, and they now move the same way.

Each import now forgets the macros it carried once it has finished, so the next preview reads your own macro.

It now shows after your macros, marked not in /macro, and you can untick it. An unticked one keeps its row until you save or open another sequence, so you can tick it again.

items.markdown: **A sequence you make with New or `/gems create` is yours from the moment you make it.** Exporting or sending one before its first save said an unknown author had written it, not you, and asked whether to share it anyway. A sequence made with New also didn't stay yours if you reloaded or logged out before that save. The next login marked it as imported, so EMS asked you to confirm before sharing your own sequence and never signed it. EMS now signs it as yours when you make it. Since it's yours from the start, the editor no longer shows the author picker for it, so you can't pick an alt's name or a pseudonym for it before its first save. It takes your pseudonym if your Default privacy mode for new sequences is Pseudonymous and you've set one, and your character's name otherwise. Its first save now adds an "edited" entry to its history, so after one save someone who imports it sees Modified where v2.4.20 showed Verified.

items.markdown: **A sequence no longer takes over another sequence's button.** A sequence called `Fury v2` and the first modifier variant of a sequence called `Fury` had the same button name, so whichever loaded second took the other's place, and holding the modifier on Fury's key could play Fury v2. Now the sequence keeps its button, and chat says the variant has none. Two saved sequences whose names differ only in characters a button name leaves out, such as `Fury` and `Fury!`, shared a button the same way. At login the one EMS loaded last took it, and the game doesn't hand your saved sequences back in the same order every time, so which one ran could change after a /reload. Now the one whose name sorts first keeps the button at every login, and chat says the other doesn't run. If that one is disabled, made for another class or damaged, the other one runs instead. EMS also refuses a name that would share a button when you make, rename, fork or import a sequence. A sequence saved earlier under a name EMS uses for itself, such as `OOCEvent`, switched that part of EMS off; it now stays in your list without running until you rename it.

The Source tab's button kept reading Edit while your text was open for editing, and clicking it applied your changes. Now a variant's button reads Remove while the variant is there, and the Source tab's button reads Apply while you're editing.

items.markdown: **A macro of your own that clicks a sequence's button stays yours.** EMS could take a character macro that clicked a sequence's button with `/click` for that sequence's own macro, even one you wrote to cast something first. When yours came before the sequence's macro in the game's macro window, each login replaced your macro's text with the sequence's, and deleting, renaming or disabling the sequence deleted yours and kept EMS's. Clean Orphans in the Macros tab deleted it the same way once the sequence was gone. When the sequence had no macro of its own, EMS used yours at login and made none. An import that brought a macro with the same name as yours wrote over it, and the import preview didn't offer to rename it. EMS now counts a macro as a sequence's only when EMS named it, with a name starting `GEMS:`, and leaves yours alone.

items.markdown: **The Steps tab shows the spell the game casts right after you save or rename a sequence, or rename a variable it uses.** When a talent or a form makes the game cast a different spell for a step, the Steps tab shows that spell's name. A step saved with new text, and every step of a sequence you renamed, showed the spell's own name instead until something else brought the tab up to date, such as the end of your next combat or a spec, talent or form change. After you renamed a variable, a step using it showed the spell's own name as well, and once the tab caught up, every step of the version in use that named it showed the variable's old name. The display never changed what was cast. The tab now catches up half a second after the save or the rename, or when combat ends if you're in combat.

Both now reach the game unless the keyboard cursor presses something. Enter no longer presses the button under the keyboard cursor in those windows, and Space still does. Enter in a dialog's own text box still accepts the dialog. Space on that text box put you in the box and typed a space there, and now it only puts you in the box. In the export window Space on a text box now puts you in that box. On EMS's pages in the game's Options window Space made no jump either. There it now reaches the game unless the keyboard cursor is on a setting Space can press, such as a checkbox, a menu, a text box or a button. In the spell picker Space works the same way now, and Enter still starts a new line in the macro you're writing. Space on a conditional there, such as `[mod:shift]`, put a space in your macro after the conditional, and now it adds the conditional alone. Space on Insert beside the picker's Custom box did the same after that box's text, and now it adds the text alone.

items.lead: Tab completion in a popup editor fills in the popup.
items.body: The menu Tab opens in a popup editor's step box, for a spell, a variable or a sequence, opened under the main editor instead. If a step was selected in the main editor, the popup's step, completed, replaced it and marked the main editor unsaved. The popup's box showed the completed word, but the popup kept what you had typed, so saving the popup stored the unfinished word. The menu now opens under the popup's box, and a pick changes only that popup's step.

items.markdown: **Switching a popup editor to another version no longer saves the first version's action tree into it.** In a popup opened on a sequence whose version is built as an action tree, picking a version without one from the version button, editing a step and saving gave that version the action tree of the version the popup opened on. The popup now keeps each version's own tree, or none.
items.lead: Switching a popup editor to another version no longer saves the first version's action tree into it.

items.markdown: **A popup editor you close with Escape in combat gives its place back.** EMS keeps up to four popup editors open. One with no unsaved changes, closed by Escape in combat, still counted as open, and with four of those closed, opening another said you had hit the editor window limit with none on screen. A popup with unsaved changes asks whether to save them before it closes. Choosing Save there in combat closed the popup and threw your changes away. It now prints "Unavailable during combat", the line the Save button's tooltip shows in a fight, and keeps the popup open with your changes.

It now prints "Unavailable during combat", the line the Save button's tooltip shows in a fight, and keeps the popup open with your changes.

items.markdown: **A colour code you type into a step stays as you typed it.** Clicking into the step box in the editor, or accepting a Tab completion there, cut a colour code you had typed, such as `|cffff0000` and `|r` in a `/run print` line, down to stray `|` characters. The first key you typed next, or the completion, put the cut text into the step, and Save kept it that way. Applying the Source tab did the same to every step holding a typed colour code. EMS now keeps a colour code you typed.

items.markdown: **A variable in a `/cast` is no longer called an unknown spell.** A `/cast`, `/use`, `/castsequence` or `/castrandom` whose spell is a variable, such as `/cast ~MyVar~`, or holds one, was looked up as a spell name. Repair listed it as an Unknown spell error, the sequence list's health badge dropped for it, and the export and send warnings counted it, so it could ask whether to export or send anyway on its own. The Steps tab coloured the step's number red and its tooltip said `Not found: ~MyVar~`, and the import window counted it among spells that may be invalid. A `#showtooltip ~MyVar~` line was listed in Repair as a stale tooltip. A misspelled spell in a line of its own, or after a `;`, is still reported.

items.markdown: **The import line and the export and send warnings count the sequence's own problems.** After an import, the chat line's issue count also counted things the Repair window never lists, such as the sequence being open in the editor, a variable used in its steps, being in combat, or the Repair window being open. A sequence with nothing to repair could read "Found 3 issues". The warnings before an export or a send counted the sequence being open in the editor, and every selected sequence once more while the Repair window was open, so a sequence with nothing to repair asked whether to export or send it anyway. `/gems repairall` opened its window for those same rows instead of saying all sequences are healthy, and with the Repair window open it printed nothing at all, even with nothing to repair. The import line and both warnings also counted what Repair says about your own character. A sequence with no keybind and no macro made an export or a send ask, and so did every sequence while your click rate was 0. The import line and the two warnings now count what the Repair window lists for the sequence and leave out its rows about your character: the sequence's macro, its keybind, its button name, its class, spells of your class you can't cast right now, your click rate and your tap controls setting for empowered spells. `/gems repairall` counts everything the Repair window lists, so with nothing to repair it says all sequences are healthy.

items.markdown: **The keybind conflict panel checks the keys you saved to your talent loadout.** With Per-loadout keybinds on, a key saved to your active loadout, which the game binds and `/gems binds` lists, was missing from the panel you open with `/gems keys` or Check Conflicts. The spec key that the loadout replaces or turns off was checked in its place and could show as a conflict. The panel now checks the same keys the game binds, and it follows a switch of talent loadout or spec while it's open. A switch of spec with the panel open used to leave it checking the keys of the spec you'd left.

items.markdown: **The Keybind tab's Suppress in this loadout box, its Escape hint and the line under Keybinds by Spec no longer sit on other controls.** With Per-loadout keybinds on and a key saved per spec, the Suppress in this loadout checkbox sat on the left end of Check Conflicts, where a click could tick it and turn the sequence's key off in your loadout instead of opening the conflict panel. items.markdown: **Counts read right at one.** Lines that put a number before a word read wrong when the number was one, such as "Found 1 issues", "1 sequences, 1 variables", "1 versions, 1 steps", "Sequential | 1 steps" and "Modifier chain has 1 entries". The Repair window's summary and its "Fixed 1 issues" line, the step list's Loop and Pause summaries, and `/gems memcheck`, `/gems monitor` and `/gems perftest` were also in English in every language, and the Repair summary's severity counts read "2 error". Sending several sequences at once named them in English too. Each of these now reads right at one in every language EMS ships. The comparison window's tooltip for step 5 read "5 steps", and it now reads "Step 5:". The import report's two skipped lines read "Skipped: 1 (already exist)" and "Skipped 1 variable(s) (already exist).", and they now read "Skipped: 1 sequence (already exists)" and "Skipped: 1 variable (already exists)". A Key Press on a version with no steps said "Fits in all 0 steps", and it now says the version has no steps. The word after an interleave box read "steps" with 1 in the box. Most lines that hedged a count with "(s)", such as "Restored 1 keybind(s)." and "Imported: 2 sequence(s), 1 variable(s)", now take the right word for the number in every language. A few French lines still hedge their count, such as the Repair summary's count of what it can fix, and so does the Italian count of spells known but unlearned in the import window. On Korean and Chinese clients `/gems loadclass` swapped its two numbers, so its line gave the count as the class and the class as the count. Counts also take the form your language uses for each number, where every count took one plural form. In Russian a count of 2 to 4, or of 21, 22 and so on, took the form for 5 and up. French and Brazilian Portuguese now take the singular at zero as well as at one. More count lines read right at one in every language, among them the line after `/gems create`, the Steps tab's count of selected steps and the question before it deletes them, the import report's count of sequences kept for other classes, and the theme editor's question before Unsilence all.

Tab and Shift-Tab now step through a page's settings in order. On the Accessibility and CVar Health pages the number keys, Page Up and Page Down jump between sections. Space ticks a checkbox, opens a menu, puts you in a text box or presses a button. In the theme editor, Space on the Preset menu, a saved theme's Name box or the Import and Export boxes did nothing, and it now opens the menu or puts you in the box.

items.markdown: **An EMS page in the game's Options window no longer holds your action bar keys in a fight.** With one of those pages open when combat started, the number keys 1 to 9, Tab, Space and the page's other keys stayed the page's keys for the whole fight. If you closed the window during the fight, those keys stayed the page's after it too, until you opened and closed the page again or reloaded. The page now lets go of them when combat starts and takes them back when combat ends if it's still open.

The export and send warnings counted it, so they could ask whether to export or send anyway on its own. The import line counted it, the sequence list showed its warning icon and its health badge dropped, and the editor showed its spell warning and marked the step's spell as not found. Repair now lists it as Spell not learned. The export and send warnings, the import line, the sequence list's icon and health badge and the editor's spell warning leave it out, and the Steps tab marks it as not in your spellbook instead of not found. A misspelled spell is still reported, and so is a spell your class doesn't have.

items.markdown: **Make live, Unpin and Disable keep what you haven't saved in the editor.** Each of them, pressed with unsaved changes in the editor, reloaded the sequence with no prompt, so your changes and your undo history were gone. The editor now keeps them, and your next Save keeps the pin or the disable. With unsaved changes the editor also keeps them through a change made to the sequence elsewhere, and your next Save replaces that change to the version you're editing. If the editor can no longer find that version, as when it was deleted elsewhere, a line under the version bar says so, and your next Save adds your work as a new version at the end of the sequence.

items.markdown: **A Save no longer writes over another version after a change made while the main window was closed.** With the window closed, a change made elsewhere that removed an earlier version of the sequence open in the editor left the editor on the old version number, so your next Save wrote over the version that had moved into that place. The editor now catches up with such a change before it shows the sequence again or saves it, and a Save writes over no other version.

Discard now sits beside Save, and Cancel last.

items.markdown: **The Repair window's Fix All, Undo and Redo work.** Fix All fixed nothing. After you fixed one row, the next row showed [Fixed] and offered no Fix. A row you fixed and then undid kept its [Fixed] mark, and Undo after Redo left the fix in place. Each row now keeps its own mark, Fix All fixes every row it can, Undo and Redo put the sequence and the marks back as they were, and closing the window counts only the fixes you kept.

items.markdown: **Repair no longer reports an item named in a `#showtooltip` line.** A `#showtooltip` or `#show` line that names an item, such as `#showtooltip Healthstone` above `/use Healthstone`, is how a macro shows that item. When the game had loaded the item that session, Repair listed it twice: as an item in a non-/use command, a warning, and as a stale tooltip. Both lowered the sequence list's health badge, and the import line counted both. Repair now leaves such an item alone, and the editor's spell warning, when it shows for another spell, no longer lists it among the tooltip lines. The game can only look an item up by name once it has loaded the item that session, so the tooltip of an item it hasn't loaded yet is still listed as stale, as before. An empowered spell named only in a `#showtooltip` line no longer draws the channeling warning, the note that its release is available or the note about empower tap controls. Repair also checks a step stored as a list of lines, a form an import can bring in, where it skipped one. A misspelled spell in it is listed as an Unknown spell, which the export and send warnings and the import line now count, as the editor's spell warning already did, and an empowered spell in it under a channeling conditional draws the channeling warning.

items.markdown: **A step stored as a list of lines works in the editors, the Source tab and the comparison window.** A step can be stored as a list of lines, a form an import can bring in. In the Steps tab, clicking such a step stopped with a Lua error, and its row took no spell warning colour, showed no modifier badge and no tooltip, and counted its lines instead of its characters. The popup editor drew its row for it as an empty box with no count, and the game raised a Lua warning. Disabling a step, or adding a Loop, If, Pause, Embed, Interleave or macro, in a sequence holding one and then saving erased its lines. The comparison window stopped with a Lua error on it and called it changed against the same text. Applying the Source tab saved it as a line starting with `table:`, which casts nothing. The Key Press status line could say the Key Press fit such a step when it did not, the Dependencies panel missed the sequences it clicks, and an Embed step's spell and combat warnings in the Steps tab missed the spells and commands in it in the sequence it embeds. An If block holding an Embed of a sequence with such a step stopped with a Lua error, so the sequence holding the If block didn't load. Each now reads the step as the text it casts, and an Embed inside an If block casts that text too, the If's condition on each of its lines. Applying the Source tab saves such a step as that text, and so do a save after you turn a step off or add a block, a press of a step's toggle key, EMS putting the sequence's spell names into your client's language, and the repair EMS runs once at login that puts a spell's own name back where a talent's name for it was saved. Opening, checking or casting it leaves it stored as a list of lines.

items.markdown: **An item in a `/cast`, `/castsequence` or `/castrandom` that the game uses is no longer called an unknown spell.** `/cast` uses an item when the name finds no spell, `/castsequence` uses an item it names, and `/castrandom` uses an item whose spell has the item's own name, such as the Hearthstone or a hearthstone toy. When the game had loaded the item that session, as it does for an item in your bags, Repair listed it as an Unknown spell error and as an item in a non-/use command, a warning, so the export and send warnings counted it, the sequence list's health badge lost 13 points, and the editor's spell warning listed it. It now reads as the item, and the editor's preview no longer tints a step that uses an item red. Repair keeps a note for an item in `/cast` alone: an info row, which costs the badge 1 point, and whose help no longer says that items need `/use`. The import line still counts that note, and an export string, which carries how many problems Repair finds in each sequence, still counts it as a warning. A number in a `/cast` in place of an item's name now reads as an Unknown spell, an error, where it drew the item warning. An item the game cannot find by name yet, and one `/castrandom` will not use, are still listed as unknown, as before.

items.markdown: **`/gems testlocale` no longer stops with a Lua error on a step, Key Press or Key Release stored as a list of lines.** The command tries EMS's spell name translation on one of your sequences whose steps are tagged for it, and checks its step, its Key Press and its Key Release. When one of them was stored as a list of lines, the translation turned it into its text, and the command stopped with a Lua error partway through its report. items.markdown: **EMS loads on WoW Forever.** v2.4.20 stopped at a Lua error at every Forever login, because two spec functions it called are gone from that client. Nothing after that point in the login ran, so the settings panel never registered, sending and receiving sequences didn't work, and plugin sequences, the tracker HUD and the floating menu never loaded. The spell cache stayed empty for the whole session. Selecting a sequence filled in its name and icon, then stopped with an error before its steps and its Keybind, Macros, Variables, Variants and Source tabs loaded, so there was no way to bind a key to it. Every press of a sequence key after the first threw an error as well, though the cast still went off. The keybind conflict panel listed none of your sequence keys, and a spec check in a RECOMMEND expression or a custom variable always read false.

items.markdown: **Importing a bundle now asks before it skips a macro you already own.** A bundle can carry a macro whose name matches one you wrote yourself. EMS has never overwritten it, but it only told you afterwards, in chat, once the import had already run. The preview marks that macro up front and offers to bring it in under a different name. The sequence steps that point at it are updated to match. Doing nothing still leaves your macro alone. Some names cannot be renamed safely, where the name has anything in it besides letters, numbers and the underscore character, or another of your macros starts with the same words, and those are left alone with a line saying which one and why.

items.markdown: **The Key Press line now tells you where to look, and says it once.** When a Key Press is too long to fit inside some of your steps, EMS tells you so in chat. It used to repeat that on every zone change, on every spell cache refresh and on every recompile, and on a sequence with modifier variants it said it once more for each variant button, which is why it arrived two lines at a time on the same timestamp. Neither line said which button it meant. The line now names the sequence, which version, which variant and its modifier, the key it is bound to, and which steps run without it. Each button says its piece once, and again only when the answer really changes, including when you zone between two versions that fit differently.

items.markdown: **A sequence with modifier variants reports a long Key Press once, not once per button.** When your variants run the same steps and the same Key Press as the version they sit under, every one of their buttons has the same thing to say, and you were told it again for each of them. You are told once now. A variant still reports itself whenever it has something different to tell you, such as a different set of steps left out or a different count of the ones that fit. A variant with nothing different to say stays covered by that one line, no matter what it has of its own.

items.markdown: **Pinning a version on a sequence that has modifier variants takes effect straight away.** Switching the pinned version needed a /reload before the key did anything different. Until then the key fired whichever version you had just switched away from, and on some switches it cast nothing at all. A sequence with no modifier variants was never affected, and that's the reason: only the variant path swaps the buttons out instead of refreshing them, and only the refresh re-pointed your keybinds and your action bars at the new ones. Both paths do that now. Reported by Munnky on an Unholy Death Knight.

items.markdown: **The repair pass that runs when you log in no longer marks itself finished after a pass that could not read anything.** A sequence imported from someone whose talents you do not have can carry a spell your client knows nothing about. The step is uncastable, the button lights up, nothing fires, and the repair panel tells you the spell is not learned. The pass counted a step like that as fine, set the flag that says it has run, and never looked again. It now counts that step as left behind and leaves the flag unset, so it tries again at every login until the step can be resolved. A character that already spent its one attempt on an earlier build gets a fresh one. Reported through GauPanda for three affected players, and named on the original thread by itmeTeemo.

items.markdown: **Sequences imported on v2.4.14 cast nothing, and the ones already saved on your character are repaired now.** Every import on that build stored its spells as the raw `{spell:186289}` form the transport uses instead of as spell names. The sequence showed up in your list, the keybind lit up, and nothing was cast. Deleting it and importing it again gave you the same result, because the import itself was writing the damage. What kept it hidden is that each damaged copy was stamped as already being in your language: the repair panel read that stamp and reported the sequence clean, and the check that runs when you log in read the same stamp and passed over it every time. Imports store spell names again. A sequence already damaged on your character is now listed in the repair panel as an error with a Fix button, and the login check repairs it whether or not an earlier repair had cleared its stored spell tags, so anything you imported on v2.4.14 fixes itself the next time you log in. Reported by GauPanda for three players who were all holding damaged sequences, and Lionkolla ran the test that pinned it to the build.

items.markdown: **A sequence that uses another sequence as one of its steps is repaired in one pass now.** The repair rebuilt each sequence as it finished with it, so where two damaged sequences were linked, the first could be rebuilt from the second before the second had been repaired and came back holding the broken text again. That took a second login to settle. Every sequence is repaired first and rebuilt afterwards now, so one pass is enough whichever order they come up in. The message EMS prints afterwards no longer says a locale change was detected on a client whose language never changed; a repair to untranslated spell text says what it was.

items.markdown: **Your spell names survive a talent change now.** v2.4.13 stopped a save from touching versions you had not opened, and that turned out not to be where the problem was: the version you did have open was still worked out again from whatever the game reported at that moment. On a Mistweaver with Rushing Wind Kick talented over Rising Sun Kick, a step you had typed as Rising Sun Kick came back as Rushing Wind Kick and stayed that way in your saved file. Three separate things produced that one symptom. The spell recorded alongside your text is now the one your words name rather than the one your talents currently serve, so it still means what you wrote after a respec. Your step text is left exactly as you typed it when it was written on this client in this language, because there is nothing to bring it across from and a round trip through the stored spells can only change your wording. And a version you deliberately wrote for a different loadout shows the names you gave it instead of the replacement live on your character right now. Reported by Daxomault, who worked out two of the three himself and wrote a companion addon that proved them; if you installed that patch you can remove it once you are on this release.

items.markdown: **Hold While Channeling is visible on every character now.** The control only appeared if your character had an empowered spell, and the hold mode has nothing to do with empowered spells: it acts on any channel from any source. So a Demon Hunter channelling Void Ray could not reach the setting at all, because the only other way to see it was to already have it switched on. Two players ended up editing their saved variables file by hand to turn it on before the dropdown would appear for them. Release at max, the third option in that dropdown, is the only empower-specific one, and on a character with no empowered spell it behaves exactly like Hold cursor, because the hold still applies and only the release half has nothing to act on. In the ten translated clients its description now covers all three options instead of only the middle one; the English text already did.

items.markdown: **Editing one version of a sequence no longer rewrites the spells in its other versions when a talent replaces one of them.** Every save, and every quick change that persists on its own such as ticking a reset box, typing in the KeyPress or KeyRelease field, moving the reset timer or picking a step function, read back all of the sequence's versions and worked their step names out again from whatever the game reported those names as at that moment. On a character whose talents replace one spell with another, that rewrote versions you had not opened: a version holding Rising Sun Kick came back holding the replacement. Only the version you are editing is worked out again now, and it stays that way a second later when the sequence is re-signed in the background. Adding, duplicating and deleting a version, and setting which version is the default, leave the step names in the versions you already had alone. A version written in a language other than your client's is still brought across, exactly as before.

items.markdown: **The keybind conflict panel and /gems keys now also check the modifier combinations a sequence's own macro text branches on.** A sequence is bound on one key, and the panel only ever looked at that key, so a sequence whose steps or keypress text branch on shift, control or alt was reported clear while the modified key was held by something else and the branch never ran. Those combinations are read out of the sequence's own text now and checked beside the plain key, and each one another addon or a game binding holds is listed under the sequence it belongs to. A modified key nothing holds is not listed, and neither is one held by the sequence's own variant button. A key held by a different sequence whose name only starts the same way is listed rather than passed over.

items.markdown: **A sequence you wrote yourself is no longer treated as though it came from somewhere else.** A new sequence is marked as your own work the moment it is created, and the check deciding whether a sequence came from elsewhere read that mark as a sign that it had. Saving one for the first time skipped the step that records you as its author, so you were asked to confirm authorship before sending, exporting or answering another player's request for your own work, and the author name you picked in the editor was dropped instead of being kept.

items.markdown: **A sequence with one damaged version no longer breaks the version display.** v2.4.11 stopped a badly stored sequence taking the rest of the addon with it by checking each place that read one, and this release moves the check to the one place they all read from, which closes the rest of them and fixes the version number along with it. If a sequence held a version stored in a shape EMS did not expect, nothing on screen would tell you which of its versions was live: no LIVE badge in the editor, no marker beside the version in its menu, no tag on the sequence list row, and no number on the tracker, on a sequence that had a live version the whole time. The tracker also disagreed with itself, printing a number in one place and a blank in another for the same sequence, and the list and the editor disagreed the same way. Where two versions happened to hold the same value, the badge picked the wrong one and named it live. A sequence with context overrides carried one more problem: what EMS had written down about the live version and what it read back never matched, so every context change and every talent loadout change queued another reload of that sequence, on and on. All of it came from one question being answered in more than one way.

items.markdown: **A badly stored sequence no longer stops the parts of EMS that draw nothing on screen.** The same check went into four of them: answering another player who asks to see your sequence list, duplicating a sequence, activating one whose step text was stored as something other than text, and building the steps for a sequence that pulls in another sequence's steps. Each read a stored part of the sequence without checking its shape first, so steps that were not a list, step text that was not text, or a record of what a sequence had been copied from that was not a list could stop that job where it stood. The list answer had a second fault of its own: where the steps were stored as plain text, nothing stopped at all, and the count that went out was taken from the length of that text, so the player who asked was told a number of steps the sequence did not have.

items.markdown: **Collections whose sequences carry a name wrapper now import.** Some exports store each sequence in a collection as a two part package, the name followed by the sequence, instead of the sequence on its own. EMS unpacked that package when a sequence arrived still encoded and not when it arrived as plain data, and that gap sat in every route it has: the preview, the import itself, and the older migration path. A collection built the second way reported "no macro versions found" for every sequence in it. The preview named the sequences it had just read and then showed nothing, which is the confusing part: it had reached them, it just could not see inside. Nothing was wrong with those strings and nothing you already had was changed. Every route unpacks it now, so the versions and their steps come through. Reported on 26 August with two strings: the one that failed for this reason imports on this build, and the other is an encrypted sequence EMS still cannot read, exactly as before.

Older sequences can hold a keypress as a list instead, and one of those stopped the preview before it drew anything. Every part is converted before it is used now, for stored variables as well as sequences.

items.markdown: **A malformed import tells you what it could not read instead of stopping.** An import holding a version in a shape EMS did not expect could stop the preview, or get past the preview and then stop when you pressed Import. The preview lists what it could not read in the "Not imported" section with the reason and offers you the rest; a sequence still unreadable when you press Import is set aside whole, with the reason printed in chat, and the other sequences in the same paste import as normal.

items.markdown: **One badly stored sequence no longer takes the rest of the addon with it.** If a sequence ended up saved in a shape EMS did not expect, whether from an old import or a hand edited file, reading it could stop whatever was asking. That included activating it, saving it in the editor, the step count and step text on the tracker, and what another addon was told when it asked about the sequence through the plugin interface, which could stop or hand back a step count that was plainly wrong. One of these sequences could also quietly empty itself: rebuilding it read the steps back out of a shape that could not be read and wrote the empty result over the ones you had, leaving the sequence with no steps, nothing on screen to say so, and the loss still there after a reload. items.markdown: **A step could stop firing after you saved it while a temporary spell was active.** Some abilities are replaced by another while a buff or a form is up, and while that is happening the game answers questions about the original with the replacement. Blood Death Knights running San'layn hit this on Heart Strike, which is replaced by Vampiric Strike while the proc is up, and a poisoned step stayed dead for the rest of the run. Ravage on Druid of the Claw is covered as well: the game offers no route back from that one, so EMS carries a mapping measured on a live client. A step already stored the wrong way is corrected the next time EMS checks your steps, and that check no longer marks itself finished while it still has rows it could not fix, so anything it skips is retried on your next login instead of never again.

items.markdown: **Macro buttons no longer swap contents after you delete or rename a sequence.** Deleting any macro moves every macro below it up one place. EMS remembered its own macros by position and only corrected the one it had just deleted, so from that moment every other macro it owned was recorded one place too high. The next time one of those sequences changed, EMS wrote the new contents into the wrong macro and left that macro's name untouched, leaving you with a button labelled for one sequence that runs a different one, and with the sequence whose name was taken being handed a brand new macro on every reload from then on. Renaming a sequence deletes a macro as part of the rename, which is why renaming imported sequences set this off; deleting a macro yourself in the macro window did it too. EMS now finds its macros by what they contain instead of by where they sit, and it looks each one up at the moment it writes, not beforehand, so a deletion in between cannot mislead it. If it cannot find one at all it now writes nothing, instead of writing over whoever is in that place. Separately, sequences whose long names shorten to the same macro name no longer end up sharing one. EMS now checks the macro names you actually have, including macros you made yourself, so each sequence gets a name nothing else is using.

items.markdown: **EMS now asks before a sequence you did not write leaves your client.** Sending a sequence to another player, answering someone's request for one, or exporting one to a string now raises a confirmation naming the author, and nothing is sent or produced until you agree. The name shown is the person the content came from, followed back through however many times it has been copied, so a copy of someone else's work names them rather than you. Where that person cannot be identified you are told the author is unknown. Sequences you wrote yourself are unaffected: they still send, export and answer requests with no prompt. A sequence whose author marked it do-not-share is still refused outright, and no confirmation can lift that. For a batch, you are asked once and the prompt names every author in it. If a request arrives while you are in combat, nothing is sent and nothing pops up; you get one line in chat telling you a request went unanswered. The dialog is present in all eleven languages, in English until it is translated.

items.markdown: **Editing or receiving someone else's sequence no longer makes it yours.** Two things quietly transferred authorship. Opening an older sequence written by another player and pressing Save re-signed it under your name, which then let it be shared with no questions asked; that upgrade now only runs on sequences that were already yours, and an older sequence that is not yours simply keeps its old signature. Separately, a sequence arriving from another player could claim you as its original author; anything arriving that way is by definition not something you wrote here, so that claim is now discarded and you are asked before the sequence goes any further. Sequences that name their real author are unaffected and still carry them.

It was also being read as "you wrote this", so a copy of another player's sequence shared with no questions asked, which is the thing the confirmation exists to prevent. What the addon asks about now follows the content rather than the signature: if any sequence yours was copied from was written by someone else, you are still asked before it leaves. Copying your own work is unaffected and never prompts, however many times you copy it. This also holds for a copy of a copy, where the sequence you copied from was your own but the one before it was not.

items.markdown: **Undo after switching version no longer changes the wrong version.** Undo remembers a step by its position. Switching version in the popup editor swapped the working copy but kept the undo history, so pressing Ctrl+Z after a switch removed a step from the version you had just moved to, at the position it held in the version you left, and armed Save on top of it. Between two flat versions nothing stopped that reaching your saved sequence, so a version you never edited could be written back a step short. The undo history is now cleared on the switch, the same as it already was when you open a sequence or close the editor.

Only a spell that fails both checks is left alone, exactly as it is, instead of being filled in with a guess. You can retype those, and the list grows as more pairs are confirmed.

items.markdown: **Importing a sequence no longer overwrites a macro you wrote yourself.** If an import carried a macro with the same name as one already in your macro list, the addon replaced your macro's body with the imported one and started treating it as its own, with no prompt and no undo. Sequences already handled a name clash by renaming; macros did not. Now a name that belongs to a macro the addon did not create is left alone, and you get a line in chat naming it, so you can rename either side and import again. That macro is also counted as skipped in the import summary rather than reported as imported. If you import while in combat the summary is written before the work runs, so it still counts the macro as imported until combat ends and the chat line arrives.

items.markdown: **Step text stops sticking on a spell you cannot cast.** On a Demon Hunter, Reap becomes Cull in Void Meta form and Eradicate after a Void Ray channel. Leaving combat and opening `/gems` could leave one of those names sitting in the step list while the spell was not available, and it stayed there until you went back into combat and cast enough for the game to swap the spell again. Monks reported the same thing with Rising Sun Kick and Rushing Wind Kick, and the keypress box was affected as well, which is why trimming it down made the problem go away for one reporter. What the sequence actually cast was never wrong. The addon rewrites the spell names in your steps whenever the game reports that your spells changed, so a sequence written around Steady Shot reads Barbed Shot once you talent into it. That rewrite asks the game which spell is active at that exact moment, and the game answers the same way for a talent you picked as for a form you are standing in or a buff you have up, so a rewrite landing mid-fight wrote the temporary name into the step and nothing ran again once the form dropped. The rewrite is skipped during combat now, and it runs when you leave combat, when your form changes, and when the game swaps your action bar, so the name goes back on its own.

items.markdown: **Your sequence keybind survives a reload and a loading screen.** After a `/reload`, or after zoning into a delve or a dungeon, the key you set on the Keybind tab stopped firing the sequence. The key still showed correctly in `/gems`, and opening the Keybind tab and setting it to the same key again brought it back, every time. The addon re-applies sequence keybinds at runtime rather than storing them in the game's own binding list, and a loading screen drops the live binding. The code that re-applies them had been grouped with the once-per-login startup work and gated behind the same flag, so on a zone change it never ran at all. It now runs on every world load, and runs a second time shortly after the loading screen ends, which covers the window where a binding set while the screen is still up gets discarded.

items.markdown: **A panel that shows what else is bound to your sequence keys.** Open it with the Check Conflicts button on the Keybind tab or with `/gems keys`. It lists every key bound to a sequence on your current spec, plus the vehicle bar and pet battle slots, and reports four things about each one: what your saved key bindings have on it, what the keypress actually reaches, whether a modifier on that key redirects your casts, and whether a click binding holds it. Each gets its own row, including the ones that came back clean, because a check that found nothing is worth seeing too. Where the addon that made a binding can be named, the row names it and the file and line it came from. The verdict on a key is decided by what the keypress reaches, so a saved binding sitting underneath a working sequence key reads as covered rather than as a conflict. Four severity filters narrow the list, a box at the top checks any key you type, and a block headed "What this check cannot see" is on screen at all times, whether or not anything is wrong.

items.markdown: **The panel clears the conflicts it can.** Two kinds are fixable from here: a saved key binding that owns the key, and a modified-click action set to redirect your casts. Those rows get a Fix button, and Fix All does the whole list after telling you the exact number it is about to change. Undo puts back the last binding the panel changed, and if something else has claimed that key since, it leaves the key alone and says so instead of overwriting. Every fix re-reads the binding immediately before writing, so a key that moved between the check and the click is left untouched. In combat the change is queued and lands the moment you leave. The cast-redirect fix clears only the three redirect actions on that key, so shift-clicking to link an item still works. A key held by another addon's override binding cannot be taken back by any addon, and that button is greyed with a tooltip saying so.

items.markdown: **Hold While Channeling, set per version in the sequence editor.** Off is what sequences have always done: every press advances the step counter, mid-channel or not. Hold cursor stops the counter while you are channeling, so the press casts nothing and the sequence holds its place through a channel you are already running. Hold + release at max does the same and adds one thing for empowered spells: once the cast reaches maximum rank, the next press ends it there instead of letting the rest of the hold window run down. The control appears only if your spellbook contains an empowered spell, or if the sequence already carries the setting, so an import from another character does not leave an invisible flag on a character that cannot use it. The check is against your spellbook and never against your class, so any character with an empowered spell gets it. The hold by itself applies to any channel from any source. Known issue on release at max: on at least one tester's client the empower ends at the first rank instead of at maximum, on every press, with nothing on screen to say so. It does not reproduce on the development client and the cause is still open, so if your empowered casts are ending early, set that version back to Hold cursor.

items.markdown: For plugins: the API version is 4. `API:GetActiveSequence()` returns the name of the sequence the engine last drove, and the `GetAuthoredSteps` accessor that shipped in v2.3.7 is now listed in the capability set, so a plugin can find it without probing for the function. The version number now moves on any addition, not only on a breaking change, because a method added quietly mid-version left plugins with no reliable way to ask whether it was there. Nothing changes unless you run a plugin that uses it.

items.markdown: **Editing a variable takes effect straight away instead of after a reload.** Changing a variable's definition is meant to rebuild every sequence that uses it and throw away anything already built from the old definition. The listeners that do that work were reading the wrong part of the message: they took the variable's new value where they should have taken its name, so they went looking for sequences filed under a name that does not exist and found none. Nothing looked wrong and no error appeared; the old definition simply kept casting until the next reload. Creating and deleting a variable were worse, because those messages carry only a name and no value, so the listener received nothing at all and the cached copy was never cleared. All of it is reading the right part of the message now.

Its listener was reading the setting's value where it should have read the setting's name, so it never recognised its own setting: the timer kept running at whatever interval it started the session with, no matter what you set. The related option that flushes pending changes the moment you leave combat was on the same listener and never triggered at all.

items.markdown: **The automatic repairs that run when your spellbook finishes loading are actually connected now.** Six things were meant to happen the moment the game finishes telling the addon which spells you have: repairing sequences after you change the game's language, refreshing spell names after a hero talent change, the same for variables, retrying a sequence whose spell could not be looked up yet, rebuilding the sequences that use the new release-at-maximum setting, and applying a change to the sequence reset modifiers to buttons that are already loaded. All six were hooked up at the wrong moment during start-up, before the part of the addon that carries these messages had been built, so the hook-up quietly did nothing and not one of the six has ever run for anybody. They are connected at the right point now. If you have ever had a sequence stay stuck on the wrong spell name after switching language or hero talents, or needed a second reload before a sequence would work, this was why. The reset modifier setting had a second, separate fault on top of that: it was reading the setting's value where it should have read the setting's name, so even once connected it would not have recognised its own setting. That is fixed too.

That write was skipped and nothing retried it, so the setting sat unapplied while the step changes from the same edit landed normally. It is queued now and applied the moment you leave combat, reading the settings as they stand at that point rather than as they stood when you made the change, so a second edit in the same fight wins.

items.markdown: The variable sandbox reaches nine game queries under a plain name as well as their dotted `C_` form. Three of those plain names are gone in this release, because the value coming back was shaped differently from what the plain name has always meant: `GetSpellCooldown`, `GetSpellCharges` and `GetSpellInfo` each hand back a single table, where the old global of that name handed back several separate values. A variable body that read two values off one of them got the table in the first and nothing in the second, silently. All three are still reachable as `C_Spell.<name>`, which is unambiguous about which one you mean.

items.markdown: Correction to the commit that made that change, ce04bed. Its subject line also names a release-parity gate fix. That work is in the Hub tooling repo, not in this one, and none of it is in this release. Two of the reasons in its body are wrong, although the decisions they justify are right. `IsSpellUsable` is safe because no bare name of its own collides, and the predecessor name given for it is not in the current API surface either, so that is a historical assertion rather than a measured one. `IsCurrentSpell` is described as boolean before and after, which implies a bare global to compare against; there is none, only `C_Spell.IsCurrentSpell`. `GetItemCount` and `GetItemCooldown` do have live deprecated globals, as stated.

items.markdown: Saving an imported sequence no longer puts your name on it. A sequence in the older signature format upgraded itself the first time you saved, and that upgrade wrote your identity into the original-author field. When the import arrived with no signature at all there was nothing to upgrade, but the upgrade ran regardless: it bound your byline to someone else's sequence and then signed it as yours. An unsigned import stays unsigned now. Both the main editor and the popup editor were affected.

The broken entry stopped the sequence from firing when you pressed its key, threw a Lua error, and could leave EMS retrying the rebuild every few seconds. EMS now keeps the ability's name when an override does not resolve, guards the error path, and the retry stops after a few attempts and recovers on its own once spell data settles.

items.markdown: **Skyriding keybinds work even when a sequence shares the key.** If you bound a sequence to a key that dragonriding also uses, pressing it while flying fired the sequence instead of the dragonriding ability. EMS now steps aside while the skyriding bar is up, so the flight ability gets the key and the sequence binding comes back when you land.
items.lead: Skyriding keybinds work even when a sequence shares the key.
items.body: If you bound a sequence to a key that dragonriding also uses, pressing it while flying fired the sequence instead of the dragonriding ability. EMS now steps aside while the skyriding bar is up, so the flight ability gets the key and the sequence binding comes back when you land.

items.markdown: **Setting a keybind no longer jumps editor tabs.** In the sequence editor's Keybind tab, clicking Set Keybind and then pressing a number set the bind but also switched the editor to the subtab for that number. The captured key now stays with the keybind and no longer reaches the tab shortcuts, so binds to number keys (and to Delete or Enter) set cleanly.
items.lead: Setting a keybind no longer jumps editor tabs.
