items.markdown: **Long Steps lists scroll to the bottom.** A sequence with more rows than fit on screen would not scroll to the last ones -- scrolling only packed the visible rows tighter, and dragging the window bigger was the only way to reach them. Loop and If rows render a little taller than plain step rows, and the list sized its scroll range as if every row were the shorter height, so the range fell short of the real content. The list now measures each row at its true height, so long lists scroll all the way to the final step.

items.markdown: **Drag-to-reorder lands where you drop it.** When you dragged a step to a new position, the drop target was figured from a single fixed row height, so in a list with taller Loop or If rows the step could land a slot away from where the indicator pointed. Reordering now goes by each row's real on-screen position, so the step lands at the drop line -- including when you drop a row inside an If branch.

items.markdown: **Variant indicators.** Sequences that branch on modifier keys or on combat conditions now show a colored indicator on the action button so you can see which variant is active right now without checking the editor. A new Variants subtab in the sequence editor sets up per-variant behavior. The matching subpanel toggle lives in General settings.

A new Variants subtab in the sequence editor sets up per-variant behavior. The matching subpanel toggle lives in General settings.

items.markdown: **Per-loadout keybinds.** Different talent loadouts can now hold different keybinds for the same sequence. Swap loadout and the keybind set swaps with it. Set them through the sequence editor or with the new `--loadout` slash argument.

items.body: Different talent loadouts can now hold different keybinds for the same sequence. Swap loadout and the keybind set swaps with it. Set them through the sequence editor or with the new `--loadout` slash argument.

items.markdown: **Macro dependency tagging.** A native sequence can declare which other sequences it depends on. Forking a sequence carries the dependency tag forward so the chain stays intact. The Advanced Export now includes a Macros section that round-trips dependency metadata through import and export.
items.lead: Macro dependency tagging.
items.body: A native sequence can declare which other sequences it depends on. Forking a sequence carries the dependency tag forward so the chain stays intact. The Advanced Export now includes a Macros section that round-trips dependency metadata through import and export.

items.markdown: **Sequence Variables auto-reload toggle.** General settings has an opt-in toggle that reloads the UI when a sequence variable apply is queued but out of combat. The `/gems apply` slash command works for in-combat or scripted use; the empty queue case prints a clear "Nothing queued." message instead of failing silently.

items.markdown: **CVar Redo.** A Redo button sits next to Undo in the CVar Health panel. If you back out of a CVar change and then change your mind, you do not have to retype the previous value.
items.lead: CVar Redo.
items.body: A Redo button sits next to Undo in the CVar Health panel. If you back out of a CVar change and then change your mind, you do not have to retype the previous value.

items.markdown: **Hold to freeze.** A new General setting lets you pick a modifier (Shift, Control, or Alt) that pauses the active sequence while you hold it. The sequence stops on its current step and casts nothing until you let go, then continues from the same step. Handy when an auto-repeat is driving the sequence and you want to slip in a modifier-key ability without losing your place.

items.markdown: **Disable a step.** Right-click any step in the sequence editor and choose Disable Step. It stays in the list, greyed and marked "(off)", keeping its position, but is skipped when the sequence runs -- so you can A/B test a rotation with and without one step without deleting it. Re-enable it from the same menu.

items.markdown: **Settings keyboard navigation.** ESCAPE in any EMS Settings subpanel now dismisses any open EMS popup first, then closes the panel. TAB, Shift+TAB, the number keys, ENTER, and SPACE reach their targets without focus drifting to the Settings window chrome.

items.markdown: **Sidebar reload pip placement.** The "reload required" pip in the Settings sidebar now anchors to the relevant category button. It stays put when the category list scrolls instead of drifting to the wrong row.

items.markdown: **Test suite coverage of game-state-dependent paths.** The condition tests for non-player aura iteration, target debuff handling, and spell-on-cooldown lookups now widen their candidate pools (focus / pet / party units, broader spell list) and route through `/gems test prep`, which prints a one-time checklist of in-game prerequisites for full coverage. Suites previously logged five environmental SKIPs on a fresh login; after the prep walkthrough the same suite reports zero skips.

items.markdown: **Sequences survive a /reload in restricted content.** Reloading the UI inside an arena, a Mythic+ run, or a raid encounter could drop saved sequences and macros, and the loss stuck across a game restart. WoW blocks the protected setup a sequence needs for the whole restricted window; the blocked setup used to send the sequence to the corrupt-sequence prompt, whose Delete removed it for good. Sequences now stay in your saved data when that setup is blocked, and they re-arm on their own once the restriction lifts, with no second /reload needed. A one-time message tells you when sequences are paused for this reason.
items.lead: Sequences survive a /reload in restricted content.

items.markdown: **Source tab edits no longer drop data.** Editing a sequence in the Source/Raw tab and clicking Apply used to rebuild it from a limited field set, silently dropping Key Press / Key Release lines, the action tree, and context overrides. Apply now preserves the whole sequence and changes only what you edited.

items.markdown: **Author BattleTag hidden in the Source tab.** The Source/Raw tab now shows the author BattleTag as "<hidden>" instead of in clear text. The value stays stored locally (it backs author identity) and was already never included in shared or exported sequences.

Underscore names also now travel with sequence exports and convert correctly from legacy double-tilde syntax on import.

items.markdown: **False "Unrecognized spell" warning for dormant sequences.** Saved sequences for a class other than the one you are currently on no longer produce login-time warnings about unrecognized spells. Active-sequence warnings still fire when an actually-used spell cannot be resolved.

items.markdown: **Hero-talent override spells like Black Arrow.** Spells provided by a hero talent path (Dark Ranger's Black Arrow, etc.) no longer produce a false warning when the active loadout does not have the override. Non-English clients now also pick up the WoW-localized name for these spells so the macrotext matches the same way English clients do.

items.markdown: **Hero-talent spells recognized consistently after /reload.** Some hero-talent loadouts could leave a few of their spells unrecognized for a few seconds after a /reload. The recognition pass now waits for the loadout to finish loading and silently retries once if needed.

items.markdown: **Recompile failures now warn and auto-recover.** When a sequence recompile fails, EMS prints a user-facing warning naming the affected sequence and the underlying error, then attempts a silent retry. Successful auto-recovery does not print a second message.

Fork-path pseudonym default now reads the account-level
  config.privacyDefault when the fork's per-sequence privacyMode is
  unset. Phase 1.5 fixed the StampOriginal resolver but the
  DuplicateSequence -> StampForked -> StampOriginal integration path
  builds the new sequence with no privacyMode field, so the resolver
  still fell through to the current character name. DuplicateSequence
  now initializes privacyMode from config.privacyDefault (same
  fallback chain Defaults.lua uses for brand-new sequences), and
  GetDefaultAuthorChoice now treats a nil/empty privacyMode as

  author defaults for the same user configuration.

items.markdown:
Hero-talent override spells like Soul Immolation (Felscarred Demon
  Hunter replacement for Immolation Aura), Eradicate, and other
  talented override variants no longer trigger the orange "needs
  attention" warning banner over sequences that reference them by
  their override name. The spell cache only registered each spellbook
  entry under its base name, so sequences that typed the override
  name found nothing in the cache, the validator marked them
  known-but-not-in-spellbook, and the banner counted them as stale.
  The cache scan now adds a second pass that registers each active
  override variant under its own name (Soul Immolation alongside
  Immolation Aura, etc.), and the validator no longer counts
  known-not-in-spellbook spells toward the stale total -- those
  spells are legitimately castable via macros, so the warning was
  misleading even before the cache fix. The tooltip detail still
  lists them individually for diagnostic purposes.

  same locale used to skip the override heal pass; sequences that
  imported under one talent loadout and got reloaded under another
  could keep stale spell names baked into the macrotext until a

Override re-translation now runs on every spell cache refresh, not
  only when the client locale actually changed. A `/reload` with the
  same locale used to skip the override heal pass; sequences that
  imported under one talent loadout and got reloaded under another
  could keep stale spell names baked into the macrotext until a
  locale change or a talent swap kicked the heal pipeline. Real
  world reports from a Demon Hunter Felscarred user on Soul
  Immolation are the canonical repro.

items.markdown:
Sequences could go unusable for the rest of a Mythic Plus key
  after a /reload mid-run. The bootstrap step that loads keybinds
  was skipped silently when the addon-restriction lockdown was
  active (any Mythic Plus key keeps the lockdown active for the
  whole run, not just during combat). The skipped call was never
  retried, so keybinds stayed unbound until the key ended.
  Bootstrap now queues the keybind load through the out-of-combat
  queue when the lockdown is active, so it fires automatically
  when the lockdown lifts (key ends, combat drops, encounter
  finishes). Reported by Hydra on a Demon Hunter Felscarred run.

  corrupt payloads) no longer reach SavedVariables. {spell:NNN} tokens

Imported sequences now follow your current talent build across respec
  and spec change. Importing a GSE3 sequence under one talent loadout
  and switching to a different one no longer leaves stale spell names
  baked into the macrotext. The `taggedSteps` shadow form kept
  locale-portable spell IDs alongside the macrotext; the new
  `HealOverrideSteps` pass re-runs `FindSpellOverrideByID` against the
  current talent state on `TRAIT_CONFIG_UPDATED` and
  `PLAYER_SPECIALIZATION_CHANGED`, then rewrites the user-facing step
  text. Reverse direction also handled: imports made while the
  override is already active walk the `FindBaseSpellByID` chain at
  translate time so the engine has the base ID to resolve forward
  from. Strategy A from the L500 design pass; zero schema change.
  Existing pre-fix sequences keep current behavior until re-imported.
  Pershizzle's BM Hunter case (Barbed Shot via Steady Shot's base ID)
  is the canonical repro. Shipped pending real-world telemetry --
  Phase 4 in-game smoke was assumed-pass, not empirically run; please
  report anything that misbehaves on Discord.

Sequences edited during combat no longer vanish on next login. The
  OOCQueue priority for DEACTIVATE was higher than ACTIVATE, so the
  sequence-rebuild dance ran ACTIVATE first and DEACTIVATE second on
  combat-end -- the trailing DEACTIVATE wiped both the new
  SecureActionButton and the SavedVariables entry that ACTIVATE just
  wrote. Priorities swapped so DEACTIVATE runs first; the rebuild now
  lands intact. Also fixes the related "I have to /reload to see my
  edits take effect" pattern when editing during combat.

  nil value") when a sequence holds legacy table-shaped step data.
  The StepListView row initializer used the `or ""` fallback for

  defenses) reached :gmatch and crashed per visible row. Initializer
  now applies the same type-check defensive pattern already used by
  the row's display-text and spell-validator branches.

Tempo Advisor no longer throws "attempt to perform arithmetic on
  local 'haste' (a secret number value)" on WoW 12.0.5. The GetLiveGCD
  fallback path (which runs when the GCD spell-cooldown query returns
  duration 0, common during fast sequence spam) used arithmetic on
  the haste value returned by GetHaste(). WoW 12.0+ tags player-stat
  values as secret, and arithmetic on a secret value from addon-tainted
  execution raises a Lua error. Arithmetic now runs inside a pcall;
  when the secret-tag blocks the math, GetLiveGCD falls back to the
  no-haste baseline (1500ms, floor-respecting).

Sequences no longer randomly disappear after some instance
  transitions. The PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD handler reran the full
  bootstrap (sequence restore, macro-stub scan, keybind load) on
  every fire of that event, including every instance entry. The
  rebuild dance had a race window where keybinds could end up
  unbound if the OOCQueue restricted-state flicker did not align
  with the LoadKeybinds OOC gate. Bootstrap now runs once per
  addon load (gated on the pre-existing _initialLoadComplete
  flag); per-instance work like context detection still runs on
  every fire. Disable+enable still forces a fresh bootstrap.

releases.intro: IF action node, conditional builder, cross-class spell catalog, combat-blocked command warnings, authorship integrity. A new IF step type branches on a conditional expression with separate True and False child action lists. The Cond field gains a single-clause picker popup and a multi-bracket builder modal for OR groups, both routed automatically based on the current input shape. The Spell Picker grows a Custom tab for typing a partial spell name or raw ID, a spec scope dropdown for off-spec browsing, and an All Classes tab sourced from a bundled cross-class catalog. Each sequence carries an Original Author field that locks after creation plus a SHA-256 signature that detects tampering on load and at import. The export format swaps to native !EMS1!; GSE3 import compatibility stays in place one-way.

items.markdown: IF action node in the + Add menu. The node renders a Cond editbox plus separate True and False columns for child action lists. The compiler emits a bracketed `/cast [<cond>] <body>; <else body>` line per spec section 5 conventions. Child actions support every other step type already in the editor (Action, Loop, Pause, Embed, IF).

Re-opening the picker on a non-empty Cond field hydrates the tickbox state from the existing input.

Replaces every BarIntegration write to a Blizzard action button child texture with a write to an addon-owned overlay texture, completing the private-table pattern started in v2.0.1's StaticPopupDialogs migration. Adds six pcall-wrapped boolean condition helpers for user variable expressions, a picker UI to insert them at the cursor, and a Function Body tooltip listing them. Regenerates `zhCN.lua` and `zhTW.lua` from English source after a copy-paste shipped Korean text to Chinese players in v2.0.1.

Each helper pcall-wraps its underlying API and is safe to call in combat under 12.0 addon-action restrictions. Numeric variants (`HealthBelow`, `PowerBelow`, `GetBuffStacks`, `SpellCooldownLeft`, etc.) are architecturally blocked by the 12.0+ secret-value system on every reachable path tested -- see `Research/Variable_Taint_Solution_2026-05-04.md` v2.2 / v2.3 for the empirical sweep results. `GRIPEMS.IsRestricted` reads the existing `GRIPEMS.restrictions` table maintained by `Engine/OOCQueue.lua`'s `ADDON_RESTRICTION_STATE_CHANGED` handler and registers no event handler of its own. Tracked under IC-VAR-01 Phase 3a.

releases.intro: The Accessibility Release. v2.0.0 reframes EMS around the populations the addon was previously unusable for: blind and low-vision players using screen readers, players who play one-handed or with tremor, Deaf and hard-of-hearing players, players sensitive to flashing imagery, and players who need plain language and slower flow. The release adds spoken step announcements, a focus ring on every focusable widget, three palette presets plus an 8-type colorblind matrix, large-target mode at WCAG 2.5.5 AAA, and a one-click Accessibility preset that turns the lot on at once. CVar Health expands from a small panel into a 212-variable dashboard with auto-switching profiles, scoring, an onboarding modal, palette routing, and TAB / numbered-key / skip-to-issues navigation through the AceConfig focus shim. See [ACCESSIBILITY.md](ACCESSIBILITY.md) for the full feature list, the compatibility matrix, and the structural-limit notes.

releases.intro: Final stabilization pass before v2.0.0. Nine items, all backwards- compatible. The point is a clean baseline before the feature work resumes.

items.markdown: `OOCQueue`: the "replaced setting for nil" debug spam is gone. The internal dedup key was being built from `(opType, seqName)` where `seqName` was silently `nil` for three call sites that queued global settings changes rather than per-sequence ones. The queue collapsed every subsequent generic queue into the same `nil` bucket and logged a replacement notice each time. Fix is two-part: (1) the three offending callers in `Engine.lua` and `TempoAdvisor.lua` now pass stable seqName strings (`"macroResetModifiers"`, `"msClickRate"`, `"UseKeyHeldSpellErrorPollTime"`); (2) `OOCQueue:Add` rejects a nil seqName for any non-`OOC_OP_GENERIC` op so the bug cannot re-emerge from a future caller forgetting the key.

items.markdown: `TempoAdvisor`: `GRIP_EMS_CHAR.tempoOffGCD` is now patch-stamped. When the saved-variables shape from an earlier patch loads on a different build, Initialize migrates each spec entry to the `{_patch=..., spells={...}}` shape and wipes the classification cache for any entry whose `_patch` does not match the current `GetBuildInfo()` string. Prevents the stale-off-GCD-classification issues that accumulate across patches and previously required `/gems holdreset`. A new `/gems fs reset` subcommand wipes `_runtimeOverrides`, `GRIP_EMS_CHAR.tempoOffGCD`, and the internal spell-class cache for users who want to force a fresh scan.

  - The existing interleave checkbox in the detail settings bar now shows a tooltip (`GEMS_INTERLEAVE_TOOLTIP_TITLE` / `GEMS_INTERLEAVE_TOOLTIP_DESC`) explaining what interleave does and when to use it.

  - `Defaults.NodeSummary` grows an `ACTION_TYPE_ACTION` branch that emits the first macro line truncated to 40 chars with `..` suffix when longer, and appends `[IL:N]` when interval is set. Top-level action badges in the outline now show the macro text and interval at a glance.

A new `TempoAdvisor:GetEffectiveConfidence`getter derives the display label: "Calibrated" wins when Tier 3 has converged AND the sequence has no unknown spells, otherwise the theoretical label shows. Fixes a 2-3 second oscillation where the two writers were clobbering a shared `rec.confidence` field and the tooltip/overlay flickered between "Estimated" and "Calibrated". Legacy `rec.confidence` values are mapped onto the best-fit new field on Initialize (`Calibrated` -> `empiricalConfidence`, anything else -> `theoreticalConfidence`) then cleared, so the UI shows a sensible label from the first /reload onwards rather than briefly showing "Unknown". Display strings unchanged.

items.markdown: UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED off-GCD reclassifier no longer wipes the entire TempoAdvisor debounce table and re-analyses every registered sequence. A name-keyed spellID-to-sequence index (TA.\_spellToSequences) drives a scoped reanalyse that touches only the sequences referencing the spells that were just flipped to off-GCD. For spells no active sequence uses -- the common case -- the scoped helper returns immediately. Rename is handled implicitly via the existing SequenceEditor DELETED+CREATED pair; no dedicated rename event or GUID infrastructure was added. The index rebuilds on SPELL_CACHE_REFRESHED so existing saved sequences are indexed correctly once SpellCache finishes its first scan at PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD.
